Title: Tesla kills the models that put it on the map to make room for robots

Summary: 
Tesla is discontinuing production of the Model S and Model X, its flagship luxury vehicles that helped establish the company as a high-tech EV disruptor, in favor of shifting focus to autonomous technology. CEO Elon Musk announced the decision during the Q4 2025 earnings call, citing a strategic pivot toward autonomy. Model S and X production will wind down in the coming quarter and cease entirely, with Musk stating, 'It's time to bring the Model S and X programs to an end with an honourable discharge.' The Fremont, California factory space previously used for Model S and X will be converted into a factory for the Optimus robot, with a long-term goal of producing one million units annually. Tesla will also begin production of the autonomous Cybercab in April 2026. While the Model S and X were previously axed in right-hand drive markets in 2023, they remained in left-hand drive markets like the US. Tesla no longer reports Model S and X deliveries separately, combining them with the Cybertruck; in 2025, only 50,850 units were delivered across the three models, compared to 1,585,279 Model 3 and Model Y units. Musk emphasized that, long-term, Tesla will focus on autonomous vehicles, with the exception of the next-generation Roadster, expected to debut in April 2026. The Model S launched in 2012, followed by the Model X in 2015, both receiving updates over the years, including a major redesign in 2021 that ended right-hand drive production.
